newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Thin Russian shares close lower, rises expected.
newsitem.headline: Thin Russian shares close lower, rises expected.

text.p: Trading dried up on the Russian Trading System on Monday leaving leading shares slightly down and traders uncertain of short term trends but predicting the next strong move would be up.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index fell almost one percent to 468.66 on a dreary $41.23 million market turnover compared to a healthy average of $50-$60 million.

"The selling we've seen in the last 3-4 days is sporadic, quieter on the down side," said a senior Western trader. "The tone is still intact," he added predicting the next move would be up but declining to say when.

UES EESR.RTS national power utility edged down to $0.4102 from $0.4165 at the previous close. St Petersburg Telephone SPTL.RTS was one of the top gainers rising to $1.900, off a new high of $1.923, from $1.750 on Friday.
Trades said there were rumours of a forthcoming ADR issue though there was no confirmation from the telecom company.
Oil producer LUKoil prefs LKOH_p.RTS fell to $13.65 from $14.00.

"People are a bit spooked by Wall Street and increased international volatility," said Brunswick director Martin Diggle. But he said nervous long positions had sold last week. "The market seems to be holding up pretty well," he said.
"My own sense is that if Wall Street calms down, then the market can take another run at the highs."
The Dow Jones broke the 8,000 point level last week but profit-taking hit on Friday and continued into early Monday trading.
Latin American markets, especially Brazil, have also been volatile while the RTS index has eased about seven percent in 12 days after gaining about 30 percent in the previous month.
